TEAM IDENTITY & ETYMOLOGY

The team’s name StarMina HORIZON encapsulates our core mission: bridging space exploration, strategic environmental stewardship, and the technological frontier. It combines celestial science with regional industrial purpose:

•  Star (Celestial & Remote Sensing Science)

•  Mina (Arabic: مِينَاء - Port / Harbor / Safe Haven)

•  Horizon (The New Frontier of Decarbonization)
summary: As global climate strategies accelerate geological Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS), the central vulnerability remains post-injection integrity: how do we definitively prove that sequestered carbon dioxide remains permanently locked 3,000 meters beneath the seabed? Under the NASA Space Apps Challenge 'Be an Earth Trend System Detective', Project StarMina HORIZON delivers an autonomous, space-borne Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Sentinel. Operating over Malaysia's premier carbon corridor in Sarawak, our system synthesizes multi-decadal satellite observations (NASA OCO-2, OCO-3, Aqua AIRS, MERRA-2) with granular geospatial masking and MetOcean dispersion physics. By establishing empirical atmospheric baseline gradients and enforcing an autonomous 430.0 ppm containment ceiling, the Sentinel acts as an unblinking forensic investigator—discriminating between natural biosphere breathing, onshore industrial downwind plumes, and subsea reservoir containment anomalies.

1.      FORENSIC PROBLEM STATEMENT: SOLVING THE 'INVISIBLE CARBON' PARADOX

The Central Luconia carbonate province hosts the flagship Kasawari CCS project—injecting 3.3 to 3.7 MTPA of CO2. Traditional offshore surveillance relies on seabed 4D seismic surveys and acoustic piezometers. While robust for subsurface imaging, these methods exhibit temporal blindness (months to years between survey vessels) and zero atmospheric sensitivity if micro-fractures vent gaseous CO2 across the water column. Conversely, raw satellite observation over tropical maritime regions suffers from intense cloud contamination, monsoonal wind shear, and biospheric noise. The forensic challenge is clear: how to isolate true anthropogenic leakage signals from complex equatorial Earth trend dynamics without false alarms.

2.      SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE & 4-PILLAR VALUE CHAIN

The Sentinel framework decouples established national industrial infrastructure from our original digital MRV innovation, establishing a verified closed-loop decarbonization ecosystem:

3.      COMPLETE SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTATION & DIGITAL TOOLS INVENTORY

StarMina HORIZON synthesized an exhaustive, end-to-end analytical stack spanning orbital remote sensing, scientific file parsing, geospatial information systems, real-time MetOcean APIs, interactive web engineering, and assistive AI computation. The comprehensive operational matrix below details each instrument and its role:

4.      THE 'EARTH TREND SYSTEM DETECTIVE' METHODOLOGY: MULTI-TIER FUSION

To solve the challenge of atmospheric trend discrimination, StarMina Horizon engineered a 4-tier forensic detection pipeline:

• Tier 1: Global Keeling Curve Calibration (Macro-Benchmark): Ingests NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory (GML) marine boundary layer data, anchoring the 2026 global mixing ratio at ~427.8 ppm (+2.4 ppm/year secular growth rate).

• Tier 2: Regional Biospheric Sink Isolation (Onshore Spatial Mask): Utilizing QGIS 3.x and geoBoundaries (ADM1), satellite column soundings (AIRS/OCO-2) over onshore Sarawak are extracted. Sarawak's rainforest canopy acts as an active carbon sink, pulling column XCO2 down to ~420.5 ppm (-7.3 ppm vs. global mean).

• Tier 3: Offshore Marine Baseline Ground-Truthing (Local Benchmark): Extracts column soundings over the Kasawari marine perimeter (4.2500°N, 112.9800°E) via NASA Panoply and Giovanni. Lacking combustion chimneys, pristine open water exhibits an ambient baseline of ~418.1 ppm.

• Tier 4: MetOcean Vector De-Aliasing & Forensic Discrimination: Integrates live 10 m wind vectors and boundary layer physics via Open-Meteo REST API. If wind blows from the SW (210°–240°), downwind onshore industrial plumes from Bintulu are flagged. If winds are calm or NE (145°), any spike exceeding the 430.0 ppm ceiling is forensically confirmed as a subsea reservoir breach.

5.      RIGOROUS DATA BENCHMARKS & EMPIRICAL METRICS

6.      STRATEGIC IMPACT, FEASIBILITY & GLOBAL TRANSFERABILITY

• Economic & Industrial Viability: By integrating freely accessible NASA Earth Observation datasets, the Sentinel eliminates multi-million-dollar repeat marine vessel charters. It operationalizes high-cadence integrity surveillance at zero offshore footprint.

• Policy Alignment with Sarawak PCDS 2030 & PETROS: Directly supports the Sarawak Land Code (CCS Rules 2022) and the Environment Bill 2023, providing regulatory authorities with an immutable top-down verification audit trail for carbon storage licensing.

• Global Scalability: The open-source architecture (QGIS + Leaflet + NASA Earthdata API) is globally transferable to any marine CCUS hub worldwide—including Northern Lights (Norway), Porthos (Netherlands), and Gorgon (Australia).

7. EARTH SYSTEM TREND DETECTIVE ALIGNMENT (CHALLENGE MATRIX)

To directly answer the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, the Sentinel platform isolates opposing regional Earth trends across Sarawak's equatorial coastline and correlates them over time:

• Opposing Regional Trends: Separates Sarawak's onshore tropical forest
canopy sinks (~420.5 ppm) and coastal industrial emissions (Bintulu–Samalaju)
from the offshore Central Luconia marine atmosphere (418.1 ppm baseline).

• Selected Earth Science Variables: Integrates column-averaged CO₂ concentrations (NASA OCO-2/3, Aqua AIRS), atmospheric reanalysis models (MERRA-2 via Giovanni), and real-time surface wind vectors (Open-Meteo REST API).

• Temporal Visualization: Interactive Leaflet.js spatial mapping and Chart.js time-series telemetry track real-time fluctuations against historical satellite baselines.

• Forensic Trend Diagnostics: Determines what is changing(atmospheric CO₂ concentration in ppm relative to wind vectors), where it is changing (across the 4-pillar corridor spanning Samalaju, Bintulu, the 138 km subsea pipeline, and Kasawari CCS), and how much it is changing (quantifying anomalies above the 418.1 ppm baseline toward the 430.0 ppm safety ceiling, isolating landward plumes from true subsea leaks).
